web.title: ‘Awami League has always departed in humiliation and disgrace’: Shafiqur
web.description:
Leader of the Opposition and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman today described the Awami League, whose political activity remains banned, as a “club of fascists”.
“Awami League has never left power under normal circumstances. It has always departed in humiliation and disgrace,” he said while addressing a discussion at the Institution of Diploma Engineers, Bangladesh, in Dhaka’s Kakrail.
He warned that anyone following the same path would face a similar fate.
“Referendum verdict was given for a change in politics. People wanted a change that would serve the country and its people and leave no scope for anyone to become a fascist again,” he said.

“We have never bowed to injustice in the past, and we will not do so now. We will continue to fight for the people, for justice and fairness, for building a humane Bangladesh, and for bringing the perpetrators of all killings to justice,” he said.Referring to the October 28, 2006, attacks and killings involving logi-baitha (boat hooks and oars) in Dhaka’s Paltan and elsewhere in the country, Shafiqur said those responsible for killing Jamaat-e-Islami and Islami Chhatra Shibir leaders and activists must be brought to justice.

Calling for an end to violence and killings in the name of politics and urging the establishment of humane politics, Shafiqur said those involved in politics in Bangladesh must work for the welfare of the people.

web.title: Verdict against Hanif, 3 others in Kushtia 6 murders case on Thursday
web.description:
The International Crimes Tribunal will deliver its verdict in a crimes against humanity case against Awami League Joint General Secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif and three other leaders of the party over the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July Uprising on Thursday.
The International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, fixed the date on Tuesday.

The tribunal issued arrest warrants for the defendants that day and ordered them to appear before the court by Oct 14.

The tribunal appointed lawyers for the defendants on Oct 23 and set Oct 27 for the framing of charges.

web.title: Parties condemn attack on CPB headquarters, demand arrests
web.description:
Several political parties have condemned Monday night’s attack on the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) headquarters in Purana Paltan and demanded the arrest and trial of those involved.
The left-wing alliance Ganatantrik Jukto Front held a protest rally and procession outside the National Press Club on Tuesday.
Participants included Bangladesh Socialist Party (BaSaD) General Secretary Bazlur Rashid Firoz, CPB General Secretary Abdullah Al Kafi Ratan and Ganatantrik Biplobi Party General Secretary Mosharrefa Mishu.
Activists from the Bangladesh Students’ Union and Jubo Union alleged that local BNP, Jubo Dal and Chhatra Dal members carried out the attack over claims of CPB links to the Awami League, whose activities are banned.
Police said tensions arose between CPB activists and members of the BNP and Jubo Dal over the slogan “Joy Bangla”.
In a statement, the CPB said a group carrying sticks gathered outside Mukti Bhaban at 10pm on Monday, claiming that members of a “banned party” were inside.
The group attempted to break through the main gate and several people were injured when CPB activists tried to stop them, the party said.
It added that the office remained blockaded even after police arrived.
Prime Minister’s Information Advisor Zahed Ur Rahman assured reporters at the Secretariat on Tuesday that the government would take action over the incident and similar offences.
Revolutionary Workers Party General Secretary Saiful Haque said violence and intimidation against people holding different political views threatened democracy.
He urged the government to prevent such incidents from recurring.
Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal President ASM Abdur Rab and General Secretary Shahid Uddin Mahmud Swapan also condemned the incident and the reported obstruction of the burial of freedom fighter Manik Pashari in Pirojpur.
They said “Joy Bangla” was a historic Liberation War slogan, not the property of any single political party, and condemned its use as a pretext for violence.
In a joint statement, Ganoshanghati Andolon acting Chief Coordinator Dewan Abdur Rashid Nilu and Executive Coordinator Abul Hasan Rubel called for an investigation, legal action against those involved and security for political party offices and activists.

web.title: IGP’s ‘crossfire’ remarks embarrassing for govt: Rizvi
web.description:
BNP Acting Secretary General and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi today said Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir's remarks about carrying out "crossfire" with the government's permission were embarrassing for the government.
Expressing concern over the comments, Rizvi said the police chief had spoken about "crossfire" at a time when BNP, which had long campaigned against enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings, was in power.
He made the remarks while inaugurating a free medical camp in front of the BNP central office in Dhaka's Nayapaltan, marking the 48th founding anniversary of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal.

Rizvi said BNP had fought against "crossfire", enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, bloodshed and fascist rule for 17 years, and that struggle had culminated in the events of July and August 5, 2024 with the BNP later coming to power through a free and fair election.
Following Tarique Rahman's election as prime minister, people across the country expect a more humane Bangladesh, he said. Against that backdrop, the police chief's remarks about crossfire had raised serious concerns, Rizvi added.

Earlier on Monday, IGP Ali Hossain Fakir said at a programme in Dhaka's Chawkbazar that "crossfire will be carried out if necessary with the government's permission". Amid the criticism, Police Headquarters issued a clarification on Monday evening, saying the IGP had not used the term "crossfire" to suggest extrajudicial killings or punishment outside the legal process.

web.title: Bangladesh: Former PM Hasina alleges massive human rights violations under BNP rule
web.description:
Dhaka, Oct 27 : Bangladesh's former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has alleged that the country is witnessing mass arrests, searches, torture, false cases, extrajudicial killings and human rights violations, claiming that the rule of law, fundamental rights and public security have effectively ceased to exist.
In a statement posted on Awami League's social media platform X, Hasina said that Bangladesh, which won its independence through the 1971 Liberation War against Pakistan, had descended into an extreme state of impunity.

Slamming the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) government, the former PM said, "Fearful of public discontent, the ruling group that came to power through a rigged election is conducting block raids and mass searches in various areas across the country, including Gopalganj, through law enforcement agencies, leading to mass arrests."
"Between 5,000 and 7,000 people are being arrested every day. The prisons are so overcrowded that there is barely room for anyone else. Meanwhile, the torture and abuse of arrested individuals and their family members have exposed the government's authoritarian character. I strongly condemn and protest against such oppression and injustice," she added.

"Mass arrests and torture have become routine occurrences. What is deeply concerning is that the situation in Gopalganj has now spread across Bangladesh. I demand that the people of this country be guaranteed their basic rights and legal protection. On the one hand, people are fed up with land grabbing, looting, extortion, murder, rape and torture by activists of the so-called ruling and opposition parties, as well as the denial of political rights to a vast section of the population," Hasina stated.
She also accused the government of aggravating the country's economic crisis through what she described as its "predatory mentality".
"There are shortages of gas, electricity, fuel and fertiliser; investment has come to a standstill; mills and factories are closing every day; unemployment is rising; commodity prices are soaring; freedom of expression is being curtailed; people are being indiscriminately dismissed from their jobs; and countless other problems and crises have left the people disoriented and desperate," the former Prime Minister stated.
